Prealgebra · Lesson 11.3

Angles in Polygons

Solve this lesson →All lessons

You can measure a single angle, and you know how angles pair up when parallel lines are involved. Now look at the angles inside a closed shape. They are not independent of each other. Fix all but one of them and the last one is forced. The triangle shows this most clearly. Its three angles always total the same amount no matter how you stretch or tilt it, and once you see why, the same reasoning carries up to a shape with any number of sides.

Problem
In the diagram above, a triangle has two angles marked 47∘47∘ and 72∘72∘. Find the third angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The three angles of a triangle always add to 180∘180∘. Add the two you know, then see how much is left.
  • Subtract both known angles from 180∘180∘. Start with 180−47180−47, then take away the 7272.
Show the full solution
Two of the three angles are 47∘47∘ and 72∘72∘, so the third is whatever is left of 180∘180∘. 180−47−72=61180−47−72=61​ Every triangle's angles add to 180∘180∘, so knowing two of them always pins down the third.
Problem
In the diagram above, an isosceles triangle has its apex angle marked 40∘40∘. The tick marks show the two sides meeting at the apex are equal, so the two base angles are equal. Find one base angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The three angles of any triangle add to 180∘180∘. Subtract the apex angle to find how much the two base angles share between them.
  • The tick marks tell you the base angles are equal, so split the leftover evenly between the two of them.
Show the full solution
The three angles add to 180∘180∘, so the two base angles share 180−40=140180−40=140 degrees, and the tick marks make them equal. 180∘−40∘2=70∘2180∘−40∘​=70∘​ Equal sides force equal opposite angles, which is what lets you halve the leftover instead of guessing at a split.
Problem
In the diagram above, one side of a triangle is extended, forming an exterior angle of 110∘110∘. One of the two remote interior angles is 65∘65∘. Find the other remote interior angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The exterior angle theorem says an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, the two corners that do not touch it.
  • Set 65∘65∘ plus the unknown angle equal to 110∘110∘, then solve for the unknown.
Show the full solution
The exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so the missing one is 110∘−65∘=45∘.110∘−65∘=45​∘. That is the exterior angle theorem. It works because the exterior angle and the third interior angle sit on a straight line.
Problem
In the diagram above, the three angles of a triangle are marked x∘x∘, 2x∘2x∘, and 3x∘3x∘. Find the largest angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The three angles of a triangle add to 180∘180∘. Add the three marked pieces and set the total equal to 180180.
  • Once you solve for xx, the largest angle is the one marked 3x∘3x∘, so multiply your xx by 33.
Show the full solution
The three angles of a triangle add to 180∘180∘, so the marked pieces satisfy x+2x+3x=180.x+2x+3x=180. That gives 6x=1806x=180, so x=30x=30. The largest angle is the one marked 3x∘3x∘, which is 3×30=903×30=90​.
Key idea
The angles of a triangle. The three interior angles of any triangle add to 180∘180∘. To see why, draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. The other two angles appear there as alternate angles, and all three fill a straight line. Extend one side past a corner. The angle outside the triangle is an exterior angle. It forms a linear pair with the interior angle at that corner, so it equals the sum of the other two angles, called the remote interior angles. Since the three must total 180∘180∘, a triangle can have at most one right or obtuse angle. It is acute when all three are below 90∘90∘, right when one is exactly 90∘90∘, and obtuse when one is above.
Problem
In the diagram above is a hexagon. Find the sum of its interior angles. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The interior angles of any polygon add to (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘. Count the sides of the hexagon above to find nn.
  • A hexagon has 6 sides, so n=6n=6. Work out (6−2)×180∘(6−2)×180∘.
Show the full solution
A hexagon has 6 sides, so n=6n=6 in the interior angle sum (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘. (6−2)×180∘=4×180∘=720∘(6−2)×180∘=4×180∘=720∘​ The n−2n−2 counts the triangles you get by drawing every diagonal from one vertex, and each triangle carries 180∘180∘.
Problem
In the diagram above, a pentagon has four interior angles marked 100∘100∘, 110∘110∘, 120∘120∘, and 130∘130∘. Find the fifth angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A pentagon has 5 sides, so its interior angles add to (5−2)×180∘(5−2)×180∘. Work out that total first.
  • Subtract the four marked angles from that total to find the missing fifth angle.
Show the full solution
A pentagon's interior angles add to (5−2)×180∘=540∘(5−2)×180∘=540∘. Subtract the four marked angles from that total. 540∘−100∘−110∘−120∘−130∘=80∘540∘−100∘−110∘−120∘−130∘=80​∘ Any polygon with one angle missing works this way, since the total is fixed by the side count alone.
Problem
The interior angles of a polygon add to 1080∘1080∘. How many sides does it have? Give the number of sides.
Show a hint
  • The interior angles of an nn-sided polygon add to (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘. Set that equal to 1080∘1080∘.
  • Divide both sides by 180180 to find n−2n−2, then add 22 to get nn.
Show the full solution
The interior angles of an nn-sided polygon add to (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘, so set that total equal to 1080∘1080∘. (n−2)×180=1080(n−2)×180=1080 Divide both sides by 180180 to get n−2=6n−2=6, then add 22 to both sides. The polygon has 88​ sides.
Key idea
Polygons and their angles. A polygon is a closed figure of straight sides. Its corners are vertices, and the angle inside each corner is an interior angle. A diagonal joins two non-neighbouring vertices. We name polygons by side count. Triangle 3, quadrilateral 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6, octagon 8, decagon 10. Draw every diagonal from one vertex and an nn-gon splits into n−2n−2 triangles, each contributing 180∘180∘, so its interior angles add to (n−2)×180∘.(n−2)×180∘. A quadrilateral gives 360∘360∘, a pentagon 540∘540∘, and each extra side adds 180∘180∘.
Problem
The diagram above shows a regular octagon with one interior angle marked. Find that angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • An octagon has 88 sides, so use the interior-angle formula for a regular polygon, (n−2)×180∘nn(n−2)×180∘​, with n=8n=8.
  • First find (8−2)×180∘(8−2)×180∘, the total of all eight angles, then split it evenly among the 88 corners.
Show the full solution
A regular polygon has equal angles, so each interior angle is (n−2)×180∘nn(n−2)×180∘​. With n=8n=8, the eight angles together add to (8−2)×180∘=1080∘(8−2)×180∘=1080∘. Sharing that evenly among the 88 corners gives 1080∘8=135∘.81080∘​=135​∘.
Problem
The diagram above shows a regular 20-sided polygon with one interior angle marked. Find that angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • A regular polygon has all its interior angles equal, so each one is the total interior angle sum shared out evenly. That total is (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘, and here n=20n=20. Work out the total first.
  • Once you have the sum (20−2)×180∘=3240∘(20−2)×180∘=3240∘ for all twenty corners, one corner is just an equal slice of it. Divide by how many corners there are.
Show the full solution
A regular 20-gon splits its interior angle total evenly across all 20 corners. (20−2)×180∘20=3240∘20=162∘20(20−2)×180∘​=203240∘​=162​∘ The formula (n−2)×180∘nn(n−2)×180∘​ is just the polygon angle sum divided by the number of equal corners.
Key idea
Regular polygons. A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal. So one interior angle is the whole interior sum divided by the number of corners. (n−2)×180∘n.n(n−2)×180∘​. A regular pentagon gives 540/5=108∘540/5=108∘ and a regular hexagon 720/6=120∘720/6=120∘.
Problem
In the diagram above, a regular pentagon has one exterior angle marked. Find that exterior angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The exterior angles of any polygon always add to 360∘360∘, no matter how many sides.
  • A regular pentagon has 5 equal corners, so split that total evenly.
Show the full solution
The exterior angles of any polygon add to 360∘360∘, and a regular pentagon's 5 exterior angles are equal. 360∘5=72∘5360∘​=72​∘ That 360∘360∘ never changes with the side count, so more sides just means smaller exterior angles.
Problem
In the diagram above, one corner of a regular polygon is shown, and each interior angle is 150∘150∘. How many sides does the polygon have? Give the number of sides.
Show a hint
  • At each corner the interior angle and the exterior angle sit on a straight line, so they add to 180∘180∘. Find the exterior angle first.
  • Walking once around a polygon, the exterior angles add up to 360∘360∘. Divide that total by one exterior angle to count the corners.
Show the full solution
The interior and exterior angle at a corner form a straight line, so the exterior angle is 180∘−150∘=30∘180∘−150∘=30∘. The exterior angles of any polygon add to 360∘360∘, and here they are all equal, son=360∘30∘=12.n=30∘360∘​=12​.
Key idea
The sum of the exterior angles. Walk once around any convex polygon, turning at each corner by its exterior angle, and the turns add to one full turn. So the exterior angles always add to 360∘360∘, whatever the side count. On a regular nn-gon they are equal, so each is 360∘nn360∘​. An exterior angle and its interior angle form a straight line, so the interior angle is 180∘180∘ minus the exterior angle. Rearranging gives the side count from an exterior angle, n=360∘exterior anglen=exterior angle360∘​.
Fun fact
Bees build their honeycombs out of regular hexagons, and there is a reason. Only three regular shapes tile a flat surface with no gaps, the triangle, the square, and the hexagon. Of those three, the hexagon walls off the most space for the least wall, so a honeycomb full of hexagons stores the most honey using the least wax. Bees found the best answer long before anyone could prove it. Mathematicians only finished proving the hexagon really is the best possible in 1999.
Problem
In the diagram above, a regular pentagon and a regular hexagon share a side and meet at a point, leaving a gap. Find the gap angle marked at that point. Give the number of degrees.
Show a hint
  • The three angles around the shared point make a full turn, so they add to 360∘360∘. Two of them are the corner angles of the polygons.
  • A regular pentagon has interior angle (5−2)×180∘55(5−2)×180∘​ and a regular hexagon (6−2)×180∘66(6−2)×180∘​. Subtract both from 360∘360∘.
Show the full solution
The pentagon's corner is (5−2)×180∘5=108∘5(5−2)×180∘​=108∘ and the hexagon's is (6−2)×180∘6=120∘6(6−2)×180∘​=120∘. The three angles around the shared point make a full turn, so the gap is what is left. 360∘−108∘−120∘=132∘360∘−108∘−120∘=132​∘ Since 108+120108+120 falls short of 360360, a pentagon and a hexagon can never tile a flat surface together around a point.
Problem
In the diagram above, one corner of a regular polygon is shown where each interior angle is 44 times its exterior angle. How many sides does the polygon have? Give the number of sides.
Show a hint
  • At any corner the interior and exterior angle sit on a straight line, so they add to 180∘180∘. Call the exterior angle ee and write the interior angle as 4e4e.
  • Once you know one exterior angle, the number of sides comes from 360∘n=en360∘​=e.
Show the full solution
The interior and exterior angle at a corner form a linear pair, so they add to 180∘180∘. The interior angle is 44 times the exterior angle, so with exterior angle ee, 4e+e=180∘,5e=180∘,e=36∘.4e+e=180∘,5e=180∘,e=36∘. Every exterior angle of a regular polygon is 360∘nn360∘​, so 360∘n=36∘n360∘​=36∘, which gives n=10n=10​.

Practice these ideas

Practice
In the diagram above, a triangle has angles 55∘55∘ and 80∘80∘. Find the third angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
Two angles are 55∘55∘ and 80∘80∘, so the third is what is left of 180∘180∘. 180∘−55∘−80∘=45180∘−55∘−80∘=45​
Practice
In the diagram above, an isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 100∘100∘, and the tick marks show that the two base angles are equal. Find one base angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The angles in a triangle add to 180∘180∘, so the two base angles together make 180∘−100∘=80∘180∘−100∘=80∘. The tick marks tell us those base angles are equal, so each one is half of that. 80∘2=40280∘​=40​
Practice
In the diagram above, one side of a triangle is extended to make an exterior angle of 125∘125∘. One of the two remote interior angles is 60∘60∘. Find the other remote interior angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
By the exterior angle theorem, an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. So the two remote angles add to 125∘125∘. One of them is 60∘60∘, so the other is 125∘−60∘=65∘.125∘−60∘=65∘​.
Practice
In the diagram above, a triangle has angles 2x∘2x∘, 3x∘3x∘, and 4x∘4x∘. Find the largest angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The angles in a triangle sum to 180∘180∘, so add the three expressions and set them equal to 180180. 2x+3x+4x=1802x+3x+4x=180 That gives 9x=1809x=180, so x=20x=20. The largest angle is 4x4x, which is 4×20=804×20=80​.
Practice
The diagram above shows a heptagon (a polygon with 7 sides). Find the sum of its interior angles. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
A heptagon has n=7n=7 sides, so use (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘. (7−2)×180∘=5×180∘=900∘(7−2)×180∘=5×180∘=900​∘ Seven sides means five triangles fan out from one vertex, and each triangle carries 180∘180∘.
Practice
In the diagram above, five of the six interior angles of a hexagon are 110∘110∘, 130∘130∘, 115∘115∘, 125∘125∘, and 120∘120∘. Find the sixth angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
A hexagon has n=6n=6 sides, so its interior angles add to (6−2)×180∘=720∘(6−2)×180∘=720∘. The five marked angles add to 110∘+130∘+115∘+125∘+120∘=600∘.110∘+130∘+115∘+125∘+120∘=600∘. The sixth angle is what is left over, so 720∘−600∘=120720∘−600∘=120​ degrees.
Practice
The interior angles of a polygon add to 1440∘1440∘. How many sides does it have? Give the number of sides.
Show the solution
By the polygon angle sum, the interior angles of an nn-sided polygon add to (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘. Set this equal to the total. (n−2)×180∘=1440∘(n−2)×180∘=1440∘ Divide both sides by 180∘180∘ to get n−2=8n−2=8, so n=10n=10​.
Practice
The diagram above shows a regular dodecagon, a polygon with 1212 equal sides and 1212 equal angles. Find the measure of one interior angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
A regular polygon spreads its interior angle total evenly across all nn corners, so each angle is (n−2)×180∘nn(n−2)×180∘​. Here n=12n=12. (12−2)×180∘12=1800∘12=150∘12(12−2)×180∘​=121800∘​=150∘​
Practice
In the diagram above, a regular polygon has 15 sides, with one interior angle marked. Find the size of that angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
The interior angles of any polygon add to (n−2)×180∘(n−2)×180∘, and a regular polygon splits that total evenly across all nn angles. With n=15n=15, (15−2)×180∘15=2340∘15=156∘.15(15−2)×180∘​=152340∘​=156∘​.
Practice
In the diagram above, a regular decagon has one exterior angle marked. Find that exterior angle. Give the number of degrees.
Show the solution
A regular decagon has n=10n=10 equal exterior angles, and the exterior angles of any polygon add to 360∘360∘. 360∘10=3610360∘​=36​ That 360∘360∘ is the full turn you make walking once around the shape, so it holds for every polygon.
Practice
In the diagram above, one corner of a regular polygon has an exterior angle of 45∘45∘, where a side is extended past the vertex. How many sides does the polygon have? Give the number of sides.
Show the solution
The exterior angles of a regular polygon are all equal and add to 360∘360∘, so each one is 360∘nn360∘​. Here that angle is 45∘45∘. 360∘n=45∘  ⇒  n=36045=8n360∘​=45∘⇒n=45360​=8​ Reading the rule backwards like this turns any exterior angle straight into a side count.
Practice
The diagram above shows one corner of a regular polygon, where each interior angle is 140∘140∘. How many sides does the polygon have? Give the number of sides.
Show the solution
The interior and exterior angles sit on a straight line, so the exterior angle is 180∘−140∘=40∘180∘−140∘=40∘. n=360∘40∘=9n=40∘360∘​=9​ Going through the exterior angle is much faster than solving (n−2)×180n=140n(n−2)×180​=140 directly.
Practice
In the diagram above, one corner of a regular polygon is marked, and its interior angle is 55 times its exterior angle. How many sides does the polygon have? Give the number of sides.
Show the solution
Interior and exterior angles at a corner form a linear pair, so they add to 180∘180∘. The interior angle is 55 times the exterior angle, so with exterior angle ee, 5e+e=180∘,6e=180∘,e=30∘.5e+e=180∘,6e=180∘,e=30∘. For a regular polygon the exterior angle is 360∘nn360∘​, so 360∘n=30∘  ⇒  n=360∘30∘=12.n360∘​=30∘⇒n=30∘360∘​=12​.
